text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rebounded 3.9% today after a sharp five-day decline that wiped out 12.85% of its value. The bounce appears tied to geopolitical tension: news of a drone attack in Kuwait and escalating Iran-U.S. rhetoric raised immediate concerns about potential supply disruptions in the Middle East, which typically pushes oil prices higher and benefits refiners. U.S. oil is currently trading at $82.24 per barrel while global crude sits at $91.80, and U.S. refineries are running at 97.5% capacity — a sign the market is pricing in tighter supply.

The five-day selloff before today likely reflected broader concerns about refining margins and demand. With both gasoline and diesel inventories elevated (217.7 million and 105.6 million barrels respectively), refiners face pressure from oversupply even as geopolitical risks periodically spike the crude price. The recent collapse of climate talks, which rejected binding fossil fuel limits, may have eased some regulatory uncertainty for energy companies — a small tailwind on top of the geopolitical support.
